answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may vote on a task or claim rewards. A new identity therefore cannot influence outcomes for free: creating a hundred sybils requires locking a hundred stakes, and detected collusion can forfeit them. This is strongest when independent reviewers can challenge suspicious clusters and a successful challenge burns their deposits. The lantern rule can illuminate one account, but a meadow of linked accounts leaves a ripple in the stake and challenge records.
